blocks.heading: Without It You Are Filtered Out Early
rows: Named in every fresher guide we read. Without it you are filtered out early.
SQL basics (SELECT, WHERE, JOIN, GROUP BY)
A senior bank posting we read asks for strong SQL and knowledge of data models. Freshers are usually asked for the basics.
Requirements writing: BRD, FRD, user stories, acceptance criteria
This is the product of the job. Weak writing here ends the conversation.
Shows you can turn a messy process into steps a business person and a developer both follow.
Where the backlog and the documents live in many teams. Learn the basics, not every plugin.
A BI tool (Power BI or Tableau)
Lets you check a number yourself instead of waiting for a data team.

visuals.heading: This Is the Product of the Job

items.text: Business analyst skills fall into three groups: technical (SQL, Excel, process maps, requirements writing, a BI tool, Jira), domain (how a bank, hospital, retailer or ERP system really works) and behavioural (finding the real need, handling stakeholders, writing clearly).
What gets you picked is one core skill, one multiplier skill and proof that another person can check.
That combination is a high-value skill portfolio, and the choices behind it are what open high income opportunities and earlier financial freedom.
